title: Local completion of a Laurent and monoid extension of a formal monoid ring
statement:
Let $(E,\mathfrak n)$ be a nonzero complete Noetherian local commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], and let $S,T$ be fine saturated monoids [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] which are sharp, meaning that their only invertible element is $0$. For any coefficient local ring $(L,\mathfrak m_L)$ and sharp monoid $P$, write $L[[P]]$ for the completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] of the monoid ring $L[P]=\bigoplus_{p\in P}L[p]$, $[p][p']=[p+p']$, at $(\mathfrak m_L,[p]:p\ne0)$. Put $H=E[[S]]$. Fix $r\ge0$ and let $U=E[z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,z_r^{\pm1}]$ be the Laurent polynomial ring: finite sums $\sum_{a\in\mathbf Z^r}e_a z^a$, with $z^az^b=z^{a+b}$ and only finitely many nonzero coefficients. Let $\mathfrak p$ be a prime ideal of $U$ containing $\mathfrak nU$. Put $W=H[z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,z_r^{\pm1}][T]$ and
$$\mathfrak q=\mathfrak pW+([s]:s\in S\setminus\{0\})W+([t]:t\in T\setminus\{0\})W.$$
Then $\mathfrak q$ is prime. Let $D=\widehat{U_{\mathfrak p}}$, where the localization [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is completed at its maximal ideal. There is a continuous $E$-algebra isomorphism, with continuous inverse,
$$\widehat{W_{\mathfrak q}}\ \cong\ D[[S\oplus T]].$$
Here $S\oplus T=S\times T$ with componentwise addition; the isomorphism sends the $S$- and $T$-monomials to their respective monomials and sends each element of $U$ to its image in the coefficient ring $D$. The residue fields of both sides identify with $\operatorname{Frac}(U/\mathfrak p)$. The cases $r=0$, $S=\{0\}$ and $T=\{0\}$ are allowed.

source.place: Tag 05GG, lemma-hathat-finitely-generated, the finite quotient identity for completion. The Laurent/monoid interchange is an agent-formulated consequence, not stated verbatim in Stacks; formal monoid models motivating it are ILO VI 1.6, printed p.70.

proof.text:
Put $P=S\oplus T$, $R=E[S]$, $I=(\mathfrak n,[s]:s
e0)R$, and $A=R[z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,z_r^{\pm1}][T]=U[P]$. The equality sends $[s]z^a[t]$ to $z^a[(s,t)]$ and has the reverse map on these basis elements. Fineness gives finite generating lists for $S,T$; their nonzero members generate the respective monomial ideals, since every nonzero element is a sum containing a nonzero generator. Thus $R,A,U$ are finite-type $E$-algebras: use the monoid generators and the $2r$ elements $z_i,z_i^{-1}$. Sharpness implies that a sum in either monoid is zero only when both summands are zero. Consequently killing all nonzero $P$-monomials defines an augmentation $A	o U$. The ideal $\mathfrak r=\mathfrak pA+([s]:s
e0)A+([t]:t
e0)A$ has quotient $A/\mathfrak r=U/\mathfrak p$, hence is prime, and $IA\subseteq\mathfrak r$.

source.place: Agent finite-sum monoid algebra calculation; preparation for Tag 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated).

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], $R,U,A$ are Noetherian. In particular $I$ is finitely generated. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal] to $H=\widehat R_I$: $H/IH=R/I=E/\mathfrak n$, compatibly with $R\to H$. Since Laurent and monoid rings are finite sums, reducing coefficients gives $W/IW=(E/\mathfrak n)[z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,z_r^{\pm1}][T]=A/IA$. Under this identification the inverse image in $W$ of $\mathfrak r/IA$ is exactly the stated $\mathfrak q$: both ideals are generated by the images of $\mathfrak p$, all nonzero $T$-monomials and $IW$; here $IW=\mathfrak nW+([s]:s\ne0)W$ and $\mathfrak nW\subseteq\mathfrak pW$. Thus $W/\mathfrak q=U/\mathfrak p$, so $\mathfrak q$ is prime and $\kappa(\mathfrak q)=\operatorname{Frac}(U/\mathfrak p)$.

Apply [lem-trf-adic-base-tensor-local-comparison] with base ring $R$, ideal $I$, finite-type $R$-algebra $A$ and prime $\mathfrak r$. Its completed base is $H$, and its base-changed algebra is $W$. Explicitly $H\otimes_R A\to W$ sends $h\otimes\sum a_{a,t}z^a[t]$ to $\sum h a_{a,t}z^a[t]$; the inverse sends $h z^a[t]$ to $h\otimes z^a[t]$. These maps respect balancing and multiplication, and are inverse on pure tensors and basis terms. Step 2 identifies the prime required by the comparison lemma with $\mathfrak q$. The lemma supplies a continuous isomorphism $\widehat{A_{\mathfrak r}}\xrightarrow{\sim}\widehat{W_{\mathfrak q}}$ with continuous inverse, commuting with $A$, and says that $W$ is Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated), existing localized completed-base comparison, first application.

proof.text: Write $C=U_{\mathfrak p}$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pC$, $B=C[P]$ and $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak mB+([v]:v\in P\setminus\{0\})B$. Augmentation identifies $B/\mathfrak b=C/\mathfrak m$, so $\mathfrak b$ is maximal. There is a canonical isomorphism $A_{\mathfrak r}=B_{\mathfrak b}$. Indeed $U\setminus\mathfrak p$ is disjoint from $\mathfrak r$, so $A\to A_{\mathfrak r}$ first extends coefficientwise to $B$. Every $f\in B$ has a common coefficient denominator $u\in U\setminus\mathfrak p$, so $f=a/u$ with $a\in A$, and $f\notin\mathfrak b$ exactly when $a\notin\mathfrak r$, by reducing the constant monomial coefficient modulo $\mathfrak p$. Hence all denominators of either local ring become units in the other. The two fraction maps are inverse and preserve $U$ and each $P$-monomial.

source.place: Tag 00CO (definition-localization), explicit common-denominator calculation; local rings in Section 07BH.

proof.text: The ring $C$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian], since $U$ is Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian] its completion $D$ is Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring], $D$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak mD$ and residue field $C/\mathfrak m=\operatorname{Frac}(U/\mathfrak p)$. It is complete by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal], since $\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated. Apply [lem-trf-adic-base-tensor-local-comparison] a second time, now to $(C,\mathfrak m)$, its finite-type algebra $B=C[P]$ and prime $\mathfrak b$. The base change is $V=D[P]$ (the basis-term tensor maps of Step 3 apply again), and the corresponding prime is $\mathfrak c=\mathfrak mDV+([v]:v\ne0)V$, since $V/\mathfrak mV=(C/\mathfrak m)[P]$. We obtain a continuous isomorphism $\widehat{B_{\mathfrak b}}\xrightarrow{\sim}\widehat{V_{\mathfrak c}}$ with continuous inverse, commuting with $B$. The lemma also gives Noetherianity of $V$.

For each $j\ge1$, the canonical map $V/\mathfrak c^j\to V_{\mathfrak c}/(\mathfrak cV_{\mathfrak c})^j$ is an isomorphism. To exhibit its inverse, write any denominator $f\notin\mathfrak c$ as $f=d+e$, where $d\in D^\times$ is its constant coefficient and $e\in([v]:v\ne0)V\subseteq\mathfrak c$. Modulo $\mathfrak c^j$ its inverse is $d^{-1}\sum_{i=0}^{j-1}(-e/d)^i$, since the product is $1-(-e/d)^j=1$. Send a fraction $g/f$ to the class of $g$ times this inverse. The fraction relation makes this well defined, and the two maps are inverse. They commute with reduction in $j$ because each is the canonical coefficient/monomial map. Taking compatible sequences therefore identifies $\widehat{V_{\mathfrak c}}$ with $\varprojlim_j V/\mathfrak c^j=D[[P]]$, with both maps continuous: the $j$th output coordinate depends only on the $j$th input coordinate.

source.place: Tags 00CO (definition-localization) and 00M9 (section-completion); explicit finite geometric-series inverses and coordinatewise limits.

proof.text: Compose the inverse of Step 3, the completion of the fraction isomorphism in Step 4, Step 5 and Step 6. This gives $\widehat{W_{\mathfrak q}}\xrightarrow{\sim}D[[S\oplus T]]$, continuously in both directions. Each comparison commutes with the uncompleted coefficient and monomial maps, so it sends $u\in U$ to its image in $D$, $[s]$ to $[(s,0)]$ and $[t]$ to $[(0,t)]$; hence it is an $E$-algebra map. Since $W,V$ are Noetherian, their prime localizations are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring] the residue field of $\widehat{W_{\mathfrak q}}$ is $\kappa(\mathfrak q)=\operatorname{Frac}(U/\mathfrak p)$ and that of $\widehat{V_{\mathfrak c}}$, hence of $D[[P]]$, is $V/\mathfrak c=D/\mathfrak mD$, the same field. All maps use empty generating lists and empty Laurent tuples without modification: $r=0$ gives $U=E$, and a trivial $S$ or $T$ contributes no nonzero monomial generators. This includes $S=T=\{0\}$.

source.place: Tags 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence), 05GI (lemma-radical-completion) and 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated); assembly and residue fields.

S6: for a denominator f=d+e, d is a unit of D and e lies in c; the geometric series inverts f mod c^j, so completed V_c = lim V/c^j = D[[P]].
